sourcedFrom: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. (UNDATED)
cleanIntro: The Millennium G2 strips on a disassembly latch like its G2C descendant, with one difference that matters: ⛔ THIS BOOK'S PROCEDURE DOES NOT PULL THE TRIGGER. Step 3 is simply "Remove the slide from the grip." If you have read a G2C procedure, that is a different pistol's book. Taurus asks for a clean after every session, regardless of how few rounds were fired.

steps.title: Magazine out, and CHECK the chamber
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out, then be certain the firearm is unloaded and the chamber is empty with no ammunition inside. Taurus prints that as an ATTENTION on the same step, not as a separate ritual.
steps.aside: ATTENTION: be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and be sure to check that the chamber is empty, with no
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release button.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY/REASSEMBLY, section 5, printed p.26

steps.title: Four fingers over the slide, draw back 1/8", latch DOWN
steps.action: Hold the pistol with four fingers over the slide and thumb on the rear of the grip, draw the slide back about an eighth of an inch, and pull the disassembly latch down with the other hand. Release the slide, then release the latch.
steps.aside: disassembly latch down. Release slide. Release disassembly latch.
steps.quote: Using the fingers draw back the slide about 1/8”. With the other hand pull
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY/REASSEMBLY, section 5, printed p.26

steps.title: ⛔ Slide straight off — NO trigger pull on this pistol
steps.action: Take the slide off the grip. That is the whole of step 3 in this book. ⚠ The later G2C manual inserts "Pull and release trigger" before this point; this one does not, and the two must not be mixed. When two books from one maker disagree about whether a trigger gets pulled, each gun follows its own.
steps.quote: Remove the slide from the grip.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY/REASSEMBLY, section 5, printed p.26

steps.title: Recoil spring off the barrel, then the barrel — strip complete
steps.action: Release the recoil spring assembly from its position on the underside of the barrel, then take the barrel out of the slide by pulling it forward and up.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling it to the front and up.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY/REASSEMBLY, section 5, printed p.26

steps.title: ⛔ Powder residue out of the barrel — brass brush for lead
steps.action: After shooting, all residues of powder must come out of the barrel and the areas next to it with an appropriate brush. ⛔ If you can see LEAD particles in the bore, they are scrubbed out with a BRASS brush drenched in oil — lead does not come out with a patch and left there it raises pressure.
steps.quote: If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CARE AND MAINTENANCE, section 6, printed p.29

steps.title: Oiled cloth over everything, then take the excess OFF
steps.action: Rub the pistol and the bore with a lightly oiled cloth. Then remove the excess: Taurus wants a thin protecting film left behind, not a wet gun. Dust comes out of every crevice with a small clean brush.
steps.aside: Also the dust should be removed from all crevices with a small, clean brush.
steps.quote: The excess of oil must be removed, but a thin protecting film should remain.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CARE AND MAINTENANCE, section 6, printed p.29

steps.title: ⛔ Clean it EVERY time you shoot — and clean the magazine
steps.action: Taurus's rule here is stricter than a round count: every time you shoot the firearm it must be cleaned, regardless of how few rounds went through it — and if you shoot more than 200 in a day, clean it every 200. The magazine is named separately and must be cleaned too.
steps.aside: The magazine also must be cleaned to keep the firearm in good operating condition.
steps.quote: Every time you shoot your firearm, it must be cleaned regardless of the number of shots fired.
steps.cite: Taurus PT 111/140 Millennium G2 Instruction Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CARE AND MAINTENANCE, section 6, printed p.29

deepAbsentReason: Taurus stops the owner at the field strip on this pistol and says where the line is: "In special conditions, such as repairs, when disassembling is necessary, it is recommended the firearm be sent to a competent gunsmith or the importer." Nothing deeper is published for an owner, and a manufacturer's published limit outranks every other tier, so nothing is borrowed from elsewhere to fill it.

cleaning.name: BARREL & ADJACENT AREAS
tasks: All powder residue out with an appropriate brush
⛔ Visible lead scrubbed with a BRASS brush drenched in oil
Bore rubbed with a lightly oiled cloth

cleaning.name: WHOLE FIREARM
tasks: Light film of good-quality oil to prevent corrosion
⛔ Excess oil removed — a thin protecting film only
Dust out of every crevice with a small clean brush

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Cleaned as part of every session's maintenance

cleaning.name: INTERVAL
tasks: EVERY time it is fired, whatever the round count
Every 200 rounds within a long day's shooting

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, pushed to its rearward position.
Spring and guide rod subassembly into the slide over the barrel, compressing the spring slightly to get it into position.
Slide onto the frame and pulled fully to the rear.
Slide catch moved upward to hold the slide back.
⛔ Cycle the slide several times, no magazine and no round chambered, to confirm the barrel / slide / frame relationship is correct.
fncheck: Reassembled: with no magazine inserted and no round in the chamber, cycle the slide several times to make sure the barrel / slide / frame relationship is correct — Taurus prints that as a numbered reassembly step, not as advice. Confirm the slide catch holds the slide to the rear.
